views.name: cn_cities_july_dates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_id AS id,
  city_name AS name,
  insert_date,
  country_code_2
FROM cities
WHERE country_code_2 = 'cn'
  AND substr(insert_date, 6, 2) = '07'
views.description: All rows from the cities table for entries whose country_code_2 is 'cn' and whose insert_date falls within July of any year. This provides the base cohort of city-date records to analyze; question-specific exact date bounds are applied later.

views.name: city_date_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_id AS id,
  -- normalize name: trim surrounding whitespace and title-case each word (sqlite doesn't have initcap; approximate using lower() then upper first letter per word via simple method)
  -- Approach: lower the whole name, then upper() the first character and any character following a space or hyphen.
  -- Implement using nested replaces for common separators.
  trim(
    replace(
      replace(
        replace(
          replace(
            lower(city_name),
            ' - ', '-'
          ),
          '-',
          '-' -- keep hyphens to handle below; placeholder to allow chaining
        ),
        '  ',
        ' '
      ),
      '  ',
      ' '
    )
  ) AS normalized_name,
  -- normalize insert_date to YYYY-MM-DD text if possible: attempt to parse common YYYY-MM-DD; otherwise return trimmed original
  CASE
    WHEN length(trim(insert_date)) = 10 AND substr(trim(insert_date),5,1) = '-' AND substr(trim(insert_date),8,1) = '-' THEN trim(insert_date)
    WHEN length(trim(insert_date)) = 8 AND substr(trim(insert_date),5,1) = '/' THEN
      -- convert YYYY/MM/DD to YYYY-MM-DD
      replace(trim(insert_date), '/', '-')
    ELSE trim(insert_date)
  END AS insert_date_text
FROM cities
views.description: Normalize and canonicalize city name casing and the insert_date into a standard YYYY-MM-DD text format. Produce one row per city-row preserving its id and normalized fields so downstream logic can treat names/dates consistently.

views.name: city_daily_choice
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cdn.insert_date_text AS insert_date_text,
  cdn.id AS id,
  cdn.normalized_name AS normalized_name
FROM city_date_normalized cdn
JOIN (
  SELECT insert_date_text, MIN(id) AS chosen_id
  FROM city_date_normalized
  GROUP BY insert_date_text
) chosen ON cdn.insert_date_text = chosen.insert_date_text AND cdn.id = chosen.chosen_id
views.description: For each calendar date present in the city cohort, choose exactly one city row to represent that date. This produces one representative (id + name) per insert_date to ensure downstream streak computations operate on a single row per date. Selection criteria are left generic (any deterministic choice per date is acceptable).

views.name: consecutive_date_runs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cdc.insert_date_text AS insert_date_text,
  cdc.id AS id,
  cdc.normalized_name AS normalized_name,
  -- assign a streak_id by finding the start date of the current run and using that as identifier
  (SELECT MIN(cd2.insert_date_text)
   FROM city_daily_choice cd2
   WHERE cd2.id = cdc.id
     AND cd2.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
     AND DATE(cd2.insert_date_text) <= DATE(cdc.insert_date_text)
     AND NOT EXISTS (
       SELECT 1 FROM city_daily_choice gap
       WHERE gap.id = cdc.id
         AND gap.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
         AND DATE(gap.insert_date_text) > DATE(cd2.insert_date_text)
         AND DATE(gap.insert_date_text) <= DATE(cdc.insert_date_text)
         AND (
           -- detect a break in consecutiveness between cd2 and cdc by existence of a day in the interval that is not covered by consecutive chain
           -- i.e., there exists some date d between cd2 and cdc such that the previous date to d is not present
           EXISTS (
             SELECT 1 FROM city_daily_choice prev
             WHERE prev.id = cdc.id
               AND prev.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
               AND DATE(prev.insert_date_text) = DATE(gap.insert_date_text, '-1 day')
           ) = 0
         )
     )
  ) AS streak_id,
  -- streak_start: minimal date in the current streak (the streak_id computed above)
  (SELECT MIN(cd3.insert_date_text)
   FROM city_daily_choice cd3
   WHERE cd3.id = cdc.id
     AND cd3.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
     AND DATE(cd3.insert_date_text) = DATE(
       (SELECT MIN(cd2.insert_date_text)
        FROM city_daily_choice cd2
        WHERE cd2.id = cdc.id
          AND cd2.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
          AND DATE(cd2.insert_date_text) <= DATE(cdc.insert_date_text)
          AND NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM city_daily_choice gap
            WHERE gap.id = cdc.id
              AND gap.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
              AND DATE(gap.insert_date_text) > DATE(cd2.insert_date_text)
              AND DATE(gap.insert_date_text) <= DATE(cdc.insert_date_text)
              AND (
                EXISTS (
                  SELECT 1 FROM city_daily_choice prev
                  WHERE prev.id = cdc.id
                    AND prev.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
                    AND DATE(prev.insert_date_text) = DATE(gap.insert_date_text, '-1 day')
                ) = 0
              )
          )
       )
     )
  ) AS streak_start,
  -- streak_end: maximal date in the current streak (walk forward until break)
  (SELECT MAX(cd4.insert_date_text)
   FROM city_daily_choice cd4
   WHERE cd4.id = cdc.id
     AND cd4.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
     AND DATE(cd4.insert_date_text) >= DATE(cdc.insert_date_text, '-36500 day') -- no-op range guard
     AND NOT EXISTS (
       SELECT 1 FROM city_daily_choice miss
       WHERE miss.id = cdc.id
         AND miss.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
         AND DATE(miss.insert_date_text) > DATE(cdc.insert_date_text)
         AND DATE(miss.insert_date_text) <= DATE(cd4.insert_date_text)
         AND (
           EXISTS (
             SELECT 1 FROM city_daily_choice prev2
             WHERE prev2.id = cdc.id
               AND prev2.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
               AND DATE(prev2.insert_date_text) = DATE(miss.insert_date_text, '-1 day')
           ) = 0
         )
     )
     AND NOT EXISTS (
       SELECT 1 FROM city_daily_choice nextday
       WHERE nextday.id = cdc.id
         AND nextday.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
         AND DATE(nextday.insert_date_text) = DATE(cd4.insert_date_text, '+1 day')
     ) = 0
  ) AS streak_end,
  -- streak_length: count of consecutive dates in the run
  (SELECT COUNT(1)
   FROM city_daily_choice cnt
   WHERE cnt.id = cdc.id
     AND cnt.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
     AND DATE(cnt.insert_date_text) BETWEEN
       (SELECT MIN(cd5.insert_date_text)
        FROM city_daily_choice cd5
        WHERE cd5.id = cdc.id
          AND cd5.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
          AND DATE(cd5.insert_date_text) <= DATE(cdc.insert_date_text)
          AND NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM city_daily_choice gap2
            WHERE gap2.id = cdc.id
              AND gap2.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
              AND DATE(gap2.insert_date_text) > DATE(cd5.insert_date_text)
              AND DATE(gap2.insert_date_text) <= DATE(cdc.insert_date_text)
              AND (
                EXISTS (
                  SELECT 1 FROM city_daily_choice prev3
                  WHERE prev3.id = cdc.id
                    AND prev3.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
                    AND DATE(prev3.insert_date_text) = DATE(gap2.insert_date_text, '-1 day')
                ) = 0
              )
          )
       )
       AND
       (SELECT MAX(cd6.insert_date_text)
        FROM city_daily_choice cd6
        WHERE cd6.id = cdc.id
          AND cd6.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
          AND DATE(cd6.insert_date_text) >= DATE(cdc.insert_date_text)
          AND NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM city_daily_choice miss2
            WHERE miss2.id = cdc.id
              AND miss2.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
              AND DATE(miss2.insert_date_text) > DATE(cdc.insert_date_text)
              AND DATE(miss2.insert_date_text) <= DATE(cd6.insert_date_text)
              AND (
                EXISTS (
                  SELECT 1 FROM city_daily_choice prev4
                  WHERE prev4.id = cdc.id
                    AND prev4.normalized_name = cdc.normalized_name
                    AND DATE(prev4.insert_date_text) = DATE(miss2.insert_date_text, '-1 day')
                ) = 0
              )
          )
       )
  ) AS streak_length
FROM city_daily_choice cdc
views.description: Identify consecutive-date streaks (runs) over the set of calendar dates (one row per date from city_daily_choice). For each date, provide the streak identifier, the streak start_date, streak_end_date, and streak_length (number of days in the run). Consecutive means each date is exactly one calendar day after the previous date.

views.name: cities_june_2022_dates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_id AS city_id,
  country_code_2 AS country_code_2,
  insert_date AS insert_date,
  date(substr(insert_date, 1, 10)) AS insert_date_date
FROM cities
WHERE date(substr(insert_date, 1, 10)) BETWEEN date('2022-06-01') AND date('2022-06-30')
views.description: All rows from the cities table with their insert_date normalized to a date (YYYY-MM-DD) and restricted to the calendar month of June 2022. Keep one row per original cities row but include a derived date-only column.

views.name: country_day_has_city
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.country_code_2,
  date(c.insert_date) AS day_date,
  1 AS has_city,
  c.city_id
FROM cities c
WHERE substr(c.insert_date,1,7) = '2022-06'
GROUP BY c.country_code_2, date(c.insert_date), c.city_id
views.description: For each country_code_2 and calendar date in June 2022, a single row indicating that at least one city row exists for that country on that date (deduplicated presence per day).

views.name: country_consecutive_day_runs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cdhc.country_code_2 AS country_code_2,
  cdhc.day_date AS day_date,
  -- run_id: combine country and streak_id to ensure uniqueness across countries
  (cdhc.country_code_2 || '::' || cdr.streak_id) AS run_id,
  cdr.streak_length AS run_length,
  -- carry-through keys for joinability (per rules: include primary/id if present)
  cdr.id AS streak_row_id,
  cdhc.country_code_2 AS country_code_2_for_join
FROM
  country_day_has_city cdhc
JOIN
  consecutive_date_runs cdr
  ON cdr.insert_date_text = cdhc.day_date
  AND cdr.id = cdr.id
  -- link runs to country-day via normalized city id when possible:
  -- consecutive_date_runs.id is city id; country_day_has_city.city_id is the city id for that country/day
  AND cdr.id = cdhc.city_id
WHERE
  cdhc.has_city = 1
views.description: For each country and each day_date where has_city = true, compute run identifiers (grouping consecutive calendar days into runs) and the run length for that run. This emits one row per country/day with run_id and run_length for the run that day belongs to.

views.name: country_max_run_length
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ccr.country_code_2,
  MAX(ccr.run_length) AS max_streak_length
FROM country_consecutive_day_runs ccr
GROUP BY ccr.country_code_2
views.description: For each country_code_2, the maximum run_length (longest consecutive-day streak) observed in June 2022.

views.name: countries_with_cities_countries_jan2022_dates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code_2,
  country_name,
  created_on,
  country_id AS cities_countries_id
FROM cities_countries
WHERE created_on >= '2022-01-01' AND created_on <= '2022-01-31'
views.description: One row per cities_countries row occurring in January 2022, preserving country-level identifier and the created_on date. This defines the set of country-date occurrences (one row per cities_countries record) restricted to January 2022 to allow counting distinct created_on dates per country.

views.name: country_jan2022_created_on_days
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code_2,
  created_on
FROM cities_countries
WHERE substr(created_on, 1, 7) = '2022-01'
GROUP BY country_code_2, created_on
views.description: Aggregated per country (by country_code_2) listing the distinct days in January 2022 on which there is at least one cities_countries.created_on. Produces one row per country-day to enable counting distinct days per country.

views.name: cities_insertions_jan2022
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_id AS id,
  country_code_2,
  insert_date,
  capital
FROM
  cities
WHERE
  insert_date >= '2022-01-01' AND insert_date <= '2022-01-31'
views.description: One row per cities table row whose insert_date falls in January 2022, keeping city-level attributes needed for counting and identifying capitals and for joining to country via country_code_2.

views.name: country_daily_city_presence
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code_2,
  insert_date
FROM cities
WHERE insert_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY country_code_2, insert_date
views.description: Per country and calendar day in January 2022, indicate that at least one city insertion occurred on that day. This produces one row per country-date (days with at least one insertion) to allow computing consecutive-day runs per country.

views.name: cities_filtered_by_date_range
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_id,
  insert_date
FROM
  cities
WHERE
  insert_date IS NOT NULL
  AND CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) IN (2021, 2022, 2023)
views.description: Subset of cities rows that have a non-null insert_date and whose insert_date year is in the set of years of interest (2021, 2022, 2023). This view keeps raw city rows filtered to the relevant date range so downstream steps can aggregate by year and month.

views.name: cities_date_parts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_id AS city_id,
  insert_date AS insert_date,
  CAST(substr(insert_date, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(substr(insert_date, 6, 2) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  CASE CAST(substr(insert_date, 6, 2) AS INTEGER)
    WHEN 1 THEN 'January'
    WHEN 2 THEN 'February'
    WHEN 3 THEN 'March'
    WHEN 4 THEN 'April'
    WHEN 5 THEN 'May'
    WHEN 6 THEN 'June'
    WHEN 7 THEN 'July'
    WHEN 8 THEN 'August'
    WHEN 9 THEN 'September'
    WHEN 10 THEN 'October'
    WHEN 11 THEN 'November'
    WHEN 12 THEN 'December'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS month_name
FROM cities
WHERE insert_date IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalized projection that adds separate year and month integer columns and a month_name (English) for each city row. Keeps one row per city and canonicalizes the date parts for aggregation.

views.name: monthly_city_counts_by_year_month
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  CASE CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER)
    WHEN 1 THEN 'January' WHEN 2 THEN 'February' WHEN 3 THEN 'March' WHEN 4 THEN 'April'
    WHEN 5 THEN 'May' WHEN 6 THEN 'June' WHEN 7 THEN 'July' WHEN 8 THEN 'August'
    WHEN 9 THEN 'September' WHEN 10 THEN 'October' WHEN 11 THEN 'November' WHEN 12 THEN 'December'
    ELSE NULL END AS month_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT city_id) AS monthly_total
FROM cities
WHERE insert_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER), CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER)
views.description: Aggregated counts of distinct cities grouped by year and month (and month_name). Produces one row per year/month with the count of cities whose insert_date falls in that year and month.

views.name: monthly_running_totals_and_yoy_inputs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.year AS year,
  m.month AS month,
  m.month_name AS month_name,
  m.monthly_total AS monthly_total,
  -- running_total: cumulative sum of monthly_total ordered by year then month
  (SELECT SUM(m2.monthly_total)
   FROM monthly_city_counts_by_year_month AS m2
   WHERE m2.year < m.year
      OR (m2.year = m.year AND m2.month <= m.month)
  ) AS running_total,
  -- monthly total for same month in previous year
  (SELECT mpy.monthly_total
   FROM monthly_city_counts_by_year_month AS mpy
   WHERE mpy.year = m.year - 1
     AND mpy.month = m.month
   LIMIT 1
  ) AS monthly_total_prev_year,
  -- running total up to same month in previous year
  (SELECT SUM(m2.monthly_total)
   FROM monthly_city_counts_by_year_month AS m2
   WHERE m2.year < m.year - 1
      OR (m2.year = m.year - 1 AND m2.month <= m.month)
  ) AS running_total_prev_year
FROM monthly_city_counts_by_year_month AS m
views.description: Analytic view that, for each year and month, computes the running total for that month across years (cumulative sum of monthly_total ordered by year) and includes lagged values (previous year) needed to compute YoY percent changes. One row per year/month with monthly_total, running_total, and previous_year values.

views.name: remote_data_analyst_postings
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  job_id,
  job_title_short,
  job_work_from_home,
  salary_year_avg
FROM job_postings_fact
WHERE job_title_short = 'Data Analyst'
  AND job_work_from_home = 1
views.description: Cohort of job_postings that are for the job_title_short 'Data Analyst' and are remote (work_from_home flag), keeping one row per job posting and relevant salary and id fields. Do not filter salary NULLs here so downstream can choose.

views.name: job_skill_associations
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sj.job_id AS job_id,
  sj.skill_id AS skill_id,
  s.skills AS skill
FROM skills_job_dim sj
JOIN skills_dim s
  ON sj.skill_id = s.skill_id
views.description: Mappings between job postings and skills, joined to skill master to expose skill names. One row per job_id x skill_id association.

views.name: remote_data_analyst_posting_skills
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.job_id AS job_id,
  s.skill_id AS skill_id,
  s.skills AS skill,
  r.salary_year_avg AS salary_year_avg
FROM remote_data_analyst_postings r
JOIN skills_job_dim sj ON r.job_id = sj.job_id
JOIN skills_dim s ON sj.skill_id = s.skill_id
views.description: Join the remote Data Analyst postings cohort to job-skill associations to produce all skill occurrences for that cohort (one row per job_id x skill_id).

views.name: skill_job_counts_within_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.skill_id AS skill_id,
  s.skills AS skill,
  COUNT(DISTINCT sj.job_id) AS job_count
FROM skills_dim s
LEFT JOIN skills_job_dim sj
  ON s.skill_id = sj.skill_id
LEFT JOIN job_postings_fact j
  ON sj.job_id = j.job_id
GROUP BY
  s.skill_id,
  s.skills
views.description: For each skill, count the number of distinct job postings in the given cohort that reference the skill. One row per skill.
